findings.problem: The two ~45-line proofs are the same argument with the interval swapped. Each takes the one-sided derivative limit L, forms h t = Re(conj L * (γ t - z₀)), and gets a one-sided neighbourhood on which t is off the partition, Re(conj L * γ') > 0 and t ∈ [a,b]. Each then extracts an Ioo and shows its closure Icc lies in Icc a b via closure_minimal and closure_Ioo. It proves ContinuousOn h on that Icc. It computes the HasDerivAt of h using the const_mul/sub/congr_deriv/re' chain, and applies strictMonoOn_of_deriv_pos. The only differences are Icc q p versus Icc p r and which endpoint gives h = 0. The continuity, derivative and strict-monotonicity block (lines 137–152 and the right-hand copy) is character-for-character identical up to renaming. Any fix to this machinery has to be made twice.
findings.proposed_change: Add a private lemma, for example `strictMonoOn_conj_proj (γ : PiecewiseC1Immersion) (L z₀ : ℂ) {u v : ℝ} (hsub_cond : ∀ s ∈ Ioo u v, s ∉ γ.toPiecewiseC1Curve.partition ∧ (starRingEnd ℂ L * deriv γ.toFun s).re > 0 ∧ s ∈ Icc γ.a γ.b) (huv : u < v) : StrictMonoOn (fun t => (starRingEnd ℂ L * (γ.toFun t - z₀)).re) (Icc u v)`. Its proof takes the current lines 137–152: closure_Ioo gives Icc u v ⊆ Icc a b, then ContinuousOn, then the derivative computation, then strictMonoOn_of_deriv_pos. Put the HasDerivAt.re' computation in it as well. The left theorem then keeps only the filter setup. After `obtain ⟨q, hq_lt_p, hq_cond⟩ := h_all` it applies the lemma with u := q, v := p, and finishes with h t < h p = 0 for t ∈ Ioo q p. The right theorem does the same with u := p, v := r and h p < h t. Each theorem shrinks to about 20 lines. No new imports are needed, since the lemma uses only tools already imported here.
findings.benefit: The analytic core of Proposition 2.2 (the real projection is strictly increasing) is stated and proved once. The left and right theorems become short wrappers that differ only in the filter and the endpoint. A future change, such as weakening hypotheses or changing the projection, is made in one place.

findings.problem: h_card_cα and h_card_βd repeat the same counting argument. A subset of the finite crossing set that omits the crossing t₁ has toFinset contained in `h_fin_cd.toFinset.erase t₁`. Then card_le_card is combined with card_erase_lt_of_mem and `omega`. Only the membership transport into the larger set differs: the restriction to Icc c α versus Icc β d. The hand-written anonymous-function membership proofs duplicate the h_fin_cα/h_fin_βd subset proofs just above (lines 560–567).
findings.proposed_change: Prove one generic lemma. For `S : Set ℝ`, `hS : S.Finite` and `t₁ ∈ S`, if `T ⊆ S`, `t₁ ∉ T`, `hT : T.Finite` and `hS.toFinset.card ≤ n + 1`, then `hT.toFinset.card ≤ n`. The proof is `Finset.card_le_card` into `hS.toFinset.erase t₁`, then `Finset.card_erase_of_mem` or `card_erase_lt_of_mem`, then `omega`. Alternatively use `Set.ncard` with `Set.ncard_lt_ncard` (not checked against this Mathlib version). Define the two subset facts once, `{t ∈ Icc c α | γ.toFun t = z₀} ⊆ {t ∈ Icc c d | γ.toFun t = z₀}` and the same for Icc β d, and reuse them for h_fin_cα/h_fin_βd and for both cardinality bounds. Then h_card_cα and h_card_βd are one-line applications of the lemma.
findings.benefit: This removes about 25 duplicated lines from the already very long induction step. It also makes the inductive decrease of the crossing count visible as a single named fact rather than two copies of an opaque Finset proof.
